Overview: The Beneteau Antares 7 is a French enclosed-pilothouse outboard cruiser designed for short coastal trips, fishing and weekend use. The Antares range prioritizes visibility, sheltered helm operation and practical cockpit access rather than traditional trawler-speed efficiency.

InlandWaterways.Summary: The enclosed cruising layout works well on inland routes; beam and air draft must be checked against route restrictions.

ExposedWater.Summary: Factory CE ratings and hull form support coastal use; loading, weather and individual boat condition remain decisive.

Accommodation and tankage are modest relative to trawler-style cruisers of similar overall length

ModelCharacter: A small single-outboard wheelhouse cruiser that packages a forward double berth, modular saloon and optional separate toilet into a legal-width 24½-foot boat. Current Cruising and Fishing trims are configurations of one Antares 7 hull.
DesignLineage: The current Antares 7 belongs to Beneteau's modern outboard Antares generation.
Cruising and Fishing profiles share one hull/model and differ primarily in cockpit and equipment emphasis.
The current generation uses a single outboard up to 200 hp.
Earlier Antares 7 generations exist and should be distinguished by year rather than merged blindly.
OwnershipCharacter: Extremely simple mechanically with one outboard and modest domestic systems. Trailerability and low marina footprint are major advantages; weather protection is good but overnight comfort is compact.

ModelCharacter: The predecessor to Jeanneau's 895 family: a compact twin-outboard two-cabin pilothouse cruiser that proved genuine family weekending could fit into roughly 29 feet without diesel inboards.
DesignLineage: The Merry Fisher 855 was introduced in the early 2010s as a larger two-cabin step in the range.
It uses twin outboards and a two-cabin arrangement rather than the simpler single-engine 795 architecture.
The Merry Fisher 895 succeeded the 855 with a redesigned hull, improved circulation and updated styling.

ModelCharacter: A rare, later-generation Marine Trader sundeck trawler documented in 2010 examples: much wider and more contemporary than the classic 38 Double Cabin, with a teak-free exterior, full-width aft master and large covered entertaining deck.
DesignLineage: Multiple brokerage and owner records document 2010 Marine Trader 38 Sundeck examples.
The documented 2010 boat uses a 14'6" beam and a single 230 hp Cummins QSB, materially different from the older 38 Double Cabin.
The model name is not present in the older Powerboat Guide Marine Trader production index, suggesting a later revival or separate import generation.
It should be treated as a distinct late Marine Trader identity, not as a renamed 1980–2000 38 Double Cabin.
OwnershipCharacter: More modern and lower-maintenance externally than classic teak-heavy Marine Traders, but the very wide beam and large interior increase dockage and systems scale. Scarcity means model-specific parts and documentation may be harder to source.

ModelCharacter: A tug-like Taiwan-built displacement cruiser from Transpacific Marine with a raised pilothouse, full protective keel, wide side decks and grain-matched teak interior. A single diesel pushes the 17,000-pound hull economically at roughly 7–8 knots.
DesignLineage: Produced from 1985–1998 by Transpacific Marine in Taiwan.
The design uses a solid-fiberglass displacement hull with full-length skeg protecting propeller and rudder.
An optional upper helm is concealed within the false smokestack on some boats.
B-Atlas previously consolidated the duplicate 'Eagle 32 Trawler' record into this canonical Transpacific Marine identity.
OwnershipCharacter: Single-diesel shaft drive and protected running gear are simple and desirable. Teak joinery, windows, tanks and legacy Ford Lehman/Perkins/Sabre components are age-related considerations; hull construction itself is straightforward and robust.
